review.summary: Phase 8 meets its offline acceptance criteria with unusually strong, machine-checkable evidence, and the attempt-05 findings were genuinely fixed rather than re-labelled. docs/checks/phase-08.json records 77 commands, all exit_code 0, source_unchanged true, bound to the exact reviewed fingerprint 3e771978…; I independently derived commands_for(8) from tools/check_phase.py (7+19+3+4+3+12+29) and it equals 77, and the recorded command list matches, so tools/review_phase.py:99-113 cannot accept a partial or stale gate. The parity matrix is complete and fail-closed: contracts/qualification.json:53-68 reports 448/448 implemented, contract-verified and option-complete with unexplainedGaps 0, and tools/qualification.py:82-119,172 refuses to emit on any missing operation, export-closure gap or unexplained live row. Export closure is bound to compilation, not prose: tools/native_exports.py:415-431 rejects any capability whose probe does not reference its claimed Rust path, and the 3,820 probes are compiled and executed from the extracted archive by scripts/check-package.py. Every review-05 fix is real and guarded — publication statements corrected (CHANGELOG.md:3-12, docs/STABILITY.md:3-5, docs/SECURITY.md:57-61) with a drift guard at tools/test_ci.py:86-107; pinned Node added to all three jobs before the uv helper (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:31-34,104-107,159-162, guarded at tools/test_ci.py:109-118); the phase runner now records timeouts, kills the POSIX process group and uses a 5,460s budget reconciled with its children (tools/check_phase.py:19-51, guarded at tools/test_ci.py:33-84,172-177); all 448 matrix rows are now crate-rooted with the module and receiver bound to real source (tools/native_operations.py:79-99); the generated consumer forbids unsafe (contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs:2); the executed probe feature set is tied to the derived export union (tools/test_ci.py:167-171); and the live policy document has one unambiguous name. docs/checks/phase-08-review05-fixes.json:9-11 records 7 regressions failing before the fixes. Supply-chain hardening is proven behaviourally: docs/checks/phase-08-uv-integrity.json:76-88 shows the pinned action actually rejecting a wrong archive digest and accepting the right one, and scripts/bootstrap-python.sh:12 hashes the installed executable before running it. Dependency audit is fresh and clean (0 vulnerabilities over 206 crates, 0 cargo-deny errors), platform labels honestly separate musl native execution from four compile-only targets, the private-material receipt is bound to this exact source (docs/checks/phase-08-private-material.json:3-8), and no unsafe or todo!/unimplemented! exists in the crate. It is 9 and not 10 because live mutation and cleanup have still never succeeded against the service, the corrected workflow has no remote execution receipt, the delivery steps (commit, clean-commit archive proofs, push, tag) are by construction still outstanding, and I found two stale phase-status bookkeeping records plus an unaddressed divergence between the immutable published 0.1.0 payload and the repository's current 0.1.0 packaged content. No blocker or high finding.

findings.description: Milestone 8's "controlled live workflows and cleanup" is still only partly satisfied. iam.scopes.create (line 212) and gateway.workspaces.provision (line 232) were both rejected with HTTP 400 and rejectionDetails carrying a null code and an empty field list, so the whole downstream chain (scope read/update/delete, absence verification, workspace archival, owned-binding removal) is unexercised live, and the receipt's cleanup array is empty (line 244) with cleanupState "not_needed" only because nothing was created. No successful mutation or cleanup evidence exists for this phase; 17 of 448 operations are live-verified and 426 are unverified (contracts/qualification.json:58-66). This is recorded honestly rather than overclaimed — tools/qualification.py:27 states the cause is unestablished and that a native request-shape defect is not excluded, docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:13-20 says the same in prose, and nothing is promoted on offline parity — so it is a scope limitation, not a misrepresentation.
findings.required_fix: Keep both operations and every dependent mutation/cleanup path explicitly live-unqualified and ineligible for stable promotion. Before any stable promotion, obtain private diagnostics for the two 400 responses, reconcile the traffic-derived IAM and Gateway provisioning request contracts against a vendor specification, and record a new source-bound receipt that actually exercises create/read/update/delete plus confirmed cleanup.

findings.description: Phase 2's remote-ci-execution limitation is due_phase 8 but was never updated and its scope statement is now contradicted by this phase's own evidence. It still reads status "configured_unexecuted" with scope "Forgejo run metadata is inaccessible with available read credentials; no remote execution claim" (lines 62-68), while docs/CI.md:126-133 states a separately supplied Forgejo token now permits reading run and commit-status metadata and that run 9 executed at bde0f4e5, and docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-09.json:2-14 preserves the server-reported run with 46 successful Rust jobs and one failed contracts-and-package job. The other two phase-2 limitations carried into phase 8 were updated (resolved_in_phase_8 at line 54, qualified_with_explicit_limits at line 72); this one was not, so the limitation ledger misstates the current access and execution facts.
findings.required_fix: Update the phase-2 remote-ci-execution limitation to the actual state: run metadata is readable, run 9 at bde0f4e5 executed with 46 successful Rust jobs and a failed contracts-and-package job, the corrected workflow has no retained run, and point its evidence at docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-09.json as well as docs/CI.md.

findings.description: The phase-8 review_attempts ledger is incomplete. It lists only attempts 01-04 (lines 626-631), but docs/reviews/phase-08-attempt-05.json exists, was a real Claude Code invocation with gate_passed true and score 9 (phase-08-attempt-05.json:11-13), and is referenced only indirectly at line 828 (review_advisories source) and line 1060 (prior_check_attempts.review). PHASES.md:5-7 requires every review attempt and its result to be preserved and recorded; the canonical attempts list omitting a passing attempt makes the review-disposition history inconsistent with the artifacts on disk. The same block records milestones.claude_review as score 9 bound to attempt-04 (lines 618-624) while the newest passing review is attempt-05, which is accurate for source binding but reinforces the need for a complete attempts list.
findings.required_fix: Add "docs/reviews/phase-08-attempt-05.json" (and this attempt's record once accepted) to docs/phase-status.json review_attempts, keeping its source fingerprint and the reason it did not advance the phase.

findings.description: The repository's 0.1.0 packaged payload has silently diverged from the immutable published 0.1.0 and no policy covers it. The crate include policy is ["src/**", "examples/**", "LICENSE", "NOTICE", "README.md"] (line 11) with version 0.1.0 (line 3), so README.md is packaged; docs/checks/release-registry-0.1.0.json:70-72 records the published README.md as 4,855 bytes from source commit 4f65dc48, published 01:14:40Z, whereas the current README.md:16-20 advertises the publication and links the publication receipt that was only created at 08:05Z — text that cannot have been in the published archive. crates.io versions are immutable, so any later cargo publish from this source would be rejected and consumers of 0.1.0 see different packaged content than the repository's 0.1.0. docs/RELEASE.md:12-13 only says the v0.1.0 tag must target the published commit and docs/STABILITY.md:30-42 version policy says nothing about post-publication packaged-content changes, so a reader cannot tell that the delivered source is not the released artifact.
findings.required_fix: State explicitly in docs/RELEASE.md and docs/STABILITY.md that published 0.1.0 is immutable, that the v0.1.0 tag targets 4f65dc48 rather than the delivered source, and that any change to packaged inputs (src/**, examples/**, LICENSE, NOTICE, README.md) after publication requires a 0.1.1 version bump and a CHANGELOG entry before republication. Add a guard (for example in tools/test_ci.py next to the publication-consistency test) asserting that the workspace version differs from the recorded registry publication whenever the current packaged-candidate fingerprint differs from the published archive's file digests.

findings.description: The phase-8 delivery obligations required by PHASES.md ("push reviewed commits to origin") cannot be satisfied by, or verified in, this review: delivery.source_commit is null and source_pushed is false (lines 573-574), clean_release_archive is "pending_new_clean_commit_proofs" with only historical bde0f4e5 proofs (lines 577-583), release_tag v0.1.0 is "not_created_or_pushed" (lines 584-588), and remote_ci is "awaiting_current_reviewed_source_run" (line 566). Consistently, the gate's packaged checks ran dirty (docs/checks/phase-08-package-1.99.0.json:9,17 record requireClean false and effectiveDirty true against releaseCommit 1b81d1e). All of this is labelled accurately and the ordering is structural — the push must follow the accepted review — so this is an outstanding obligation rather than a misstatement, but the phase cannot be marked complete on this review alone.
findings.required_fix: After this review, commit the reviewed source without changing its fingerprint, run scripts/check-package.py --require-clean on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 with distinct ignored outputs and retain both only if both pass, push the ordinary commits to ssh://git@git-ssh.cdot.io/cdot/scm-sdk-rs.git, push the annotated v0.1.0 tag at the published source commit and verify its remote peel, refresh the private-material scan over the final bookkeeping, retain a Forgejo run log for the corrected workflow covering at minimum contracts-and-package and one rust matrix job, and only then record the exact commit, both archive digests and phase completion.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-08.json:1-6 records phase 8, source_sha256 3e77197835e1f9b6f56e05b775b8e8403f7449c8fe1cbf31fbe725ff8391543c (the exact reviewed fingerprint), source_unchanged true, passed true. I counted 77 recorded "command" entries and 77 "exit_code" fields, every one 0, and zero "timeout": true. I independently derived commands_for(8) from tools/check_phase.py:54-204 (phase1 7, +phase3 19, +phase4 3, +phase5 4, +phase6 3, +phase7 12, +phase8 29 = 77) and the recorded list matches, including the phase-8-only additions at lines 182-203.

tools/review_phase.py:43-60 hashes all tracked and untracked non-ignored files excluding only docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json and rejects symlinked inputs; :99-113 binds acceptance to report.passed, the exact fingerprint, source_unchanged and the complete commands_for(phase) list with every exit_code == 0; :116-142 binds the score to the preserved prompt hash, the real CLI envelope (is_error false, structured_output equal to the record) and the checks-report hash; :145-153 revalidates every earlier phase's accepted review. The prompt I received matches the generator at :205-219 including the checks SHA-256 a222061e….

contracts/qualification.json:53-68 reports operations 448, implemented 448, contractVerified 448, completeMethodOptionParity 448, liveVerified 17, liveNotVerified 431 (permission_prerequisite 3, service_contract_rejection 2, unverified 426) and unexplainedGaps 0. tools/qualification.py:82-119 raises unless all 448 unique frozen operations are present, all 3,820 export capabilities are implemented, every operation has an export binding and a source-bound hash, and :172-173 refuses to emit when any row lacks a live reason.

tools/native_operations.py:79-99 canonical_namespace now requires a crate-rooted Rust path, verifies the module path resolves to the recorded source file under crates/scm-sdk/src, and requires the receiver to appear in a struct/impl in that file; :215-216 requires each mapped method to exist as a pub fn. Every "namespace" value I extracted from contracts/qualification.json is now scm_sdk::… (airs::gateway, airs::management, airs::model_security, airs::red_team, airs::scan, airs::agentguard, shared::iam, dlp, auth), resolving the attempt-04/05 rooting finding, and the gate ran test_method_namespaces_are_crate_rooted_and_bound_to_their_source_module among 21 passing ledger tests (docs/checks/phase-08.json:248).

tools/native_exports.py:415-431 rejects any capability whose generated compile probe does not reference its claimed Rust path, and :378-382 rejects a mapped public method absent from its source; the generated consumer contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs:2 now carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)], and scripts/check-package.py:27-60 rejects any archive member outside the published include policy or matching development/credential patterns before extracting and compiling it.

tools/test_ci.py contains 19 guards, all passing in the gate (docs/checks/phase-08.json:1324): :86-107 fails if any README/CHANGELOG/docs markdown still claims an unpublished crate while phase-status records verified_existing_publication, and requires the CHANGELOG to contain the receipt's archive digest, source commit and publication date; :109-118 requires pinned setup-node before the uv helper in all three jobs; :167-171 requires scripts/check-rust.py FEATURES["native-probes"] to equal the derived requiredFeatures union in contracts/native-exports.json; :172-177 requires the phase runner's budget to cover the Rust checker's six 900-second children; :240-262 proves an unverified uv is never executed and no PATH entry is written.

docs/checks/phase-08-uv-integrity.json:76-88 preserves two actual executions of the pinned astral-sh/setup-uv action: the wrong-checksum case exits 1 with "Checksum … did not match" before extraction, and the correct-checksum case installs uv 0.13.1; :90-97 records scripts/bootstrap-python.sh verifying the installed executable digest 752a98d0… and installing Python 3.14.7 with no Python initially on PATH. .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:45-58 wires the selected digest into the action's checksum input with a fresh owned RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, and scripts/uv-integrity.cjs:16-63 fails closed on unsupported hosts, stale pins or changed bytes.

docs/checks/phase-08-dependencies.json:3-13 records a fresh RustSec head 64f92cdc (freshHead true) with pinned cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 and their binary digests; :27-52 shows 0 vulnerabilities over 206 dependencies with no ignores. Cargo.toml:12-13 forbids unsafe code workspace-wide and I found no unsafe/todo!/unimplemented! anywhere in crates/scm-sdk/src (the single "unsafe" match is the word in a doc comment at airs/gateway/helpers.rs:85).

docs/checks/phase-08-private-material.json:3-8 binds the sanitized scan to sourceSha256 3e771978…, headCommit 1b81d1e, passed true over 961 Git-visible files with 0 credential and 0 packaged-source matches. scripts/check-private-material.py:165-176 restricts only the public freshness check to source-only inputs while scan() at :90-121 still reads every Git-visible file, and scripts/evidence_common.py:172-200 shows source_fingerprint applies the same exclusions as the review gate, so the receipt hash is comparable to the reviewed fingerprint.

docs/checks/phase-08-rust-1.99.0-all.json records 25 passing test binaries (201 lib tests plus integration suites) and all six commands at exit 0; every root-level phase-08-rust-*.json shares rustInputsSha256 b15bb1a4…, so the 33 feature/toolchain runs are bound to one source state. scripts/check-rust.py:115-117 requires unchanged Rust inputs and byte-identical packaged LICENSE/NOTICE before reporting passed.

docs/checks/phase-08-review05-fixes.json:3-11 binds the review-05 fix verification to this exact source (3e771978…) and records 7 regression tests failing (exitCode 1) before the fixes, i.e. test-first evidence rather than assertion-after-the-fact.

docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-06.json:203-251 records the per-operation classifications, both 400 rejections with null code and empty field lists, an empty cleanup array, 24 service requests and 1 token exchange. tools/live_evidence.py:98-104,249-256 binds the receipt to a runtime fingerprint over crates/scm-sdk/src+examples and the workspace manifests and rejects a stale or non-zero-exit execution, so the 17 verified methods really are bound to the unchanged runtime source.

docs/PLATFORMS.md:7-20 and scripts/check-cross.py:15-48 confirm honest platform labels: Linux x86_64 musl is the only native execution host, the four cross targets are compile-only, and the checker asserts the dependency tree excludes reqwest, tokio-websockets, rustls and aws-lc-rs. The four cross reports completed in ~0.4s each because cargo found everything fresh (docs/checks/phase-08-cross-aarch64-apple-darwin.json:35 "Finished … in 0.07s"), i.e. real but fully cached compilations.

docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-09.json:2-14 preserves server-reported remote evidence for bde0f4e5 (run 9: contracts-and-package failed after 38m35s, 46 Rust jobs succeeded), and docs/CI.md:116-162 refrains from claiming a successful complete workflow for the corrected source; docs/checks/release-registry-0.1.0.json:3-31 verifies the published crates.io 0.1.0 archive and its byte-level payload equivalence except .cargo_vcs_info.json.
limitations: I used only read-only Read/Glob/Grep. I executed no check, compiled no Rust, ran no test and contacted no service, so every pass or fail I cite is the project's own retained report, not my own execution.

I did not recompute the source fingerprint 3e771978…, the checks-report hash a222061e…, or any file digest. Hash agreement between the prompt, the gate report, the receipts, the live evidence and the published archive is asserted by those artifacts; I verified internal consistency, not cryptographic authenticity. The documented trust model (repository writers and the invoked tools are trusted) applies, and I cannot distinguish an authentic run from a well-formed fabricated report.

The reviewed source is uncommitted working-tree state, so the clean-commit archive proofs, the v0.1.0 tag and the origin push for this exact source cannot exist yet and were not verifiable. I also could not run git, so statements about which files changed since 4f65dc48 rest on the supplied git status snapshot, the recorded head commit and the content of the artifacts themselves.

The corrected CI workflow has no remote execution receipt. Run 9 binds the earlier commit bde0f4e5 and consists of server-reported statuses without job logs, so the uv-integrity select step, the RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE override, the action checksum input on a real runner, $GITHUB_PATH application, --offline cache coverage for the separate contracts/native-probes lockfile and the 180-minute cold-cache budget remain unverified on a runner.

Live service evidence covers 17 of 448 operations from a single receipt on one nonproduction tenant; mutation and cleanup paths have never succeeded and the cause of the two 400 responses is unestablished. As instructed, I inspected no credential or tenant-registration file and no private diagnostics.

Native runtime evidence is limited to Linux x86_64 musl; the four other triples are compile-only and their cross reports were fully cached cargo runs, and the Linux ARM64, Apple Silicon and Windows jobs are configured without registered runners or retained execution.

I reviewed the Rust implementation selectively (workspace lints, probe consumer, adversarial/parser documentation, examples and test inventory) rather than auditing all of crates/scm-sdk; phases 1-7 were accepted by earlier reviews and I judged them only where phase 8 depends on them.

My finding that the published 0.1.0 README differs from the current README is inferred from the receipt's recorded size and publication timestamp versus the publication text now present in README.md; I could not hash the current file to prove the difference directly.
